title: State of Kerala v. Sooraj S. Kumar (Uthra Snakebite Murder Case)
crime_type: Homicide using Biological Weapon (Venomous Viper/Cobra) / Dowry Extortion
court_or_authority: Sixth Additional Sessions Court, Kollam / High Court of Kerala
legal_citation: Sessions Case No. 433/2020; Criminal Appeal No. 71/2022 (Kerala HC)
source: District & Sessions Court Kollam Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/162817291)
ipc_sections: Section 498A IPC (Cruelty by husband and dowry demand)
evidence: Scientific reconstruction experiment conducted by Herpetology Department establishing that a snake cannot naturally inflict bites through closed air-conditioned room windows
Measurement of fang puncture width (2.5 cm) on victim's arm proving forced induction and compression of snake head by human hand
Digital extraction of suspect's smartphone search history: extensive YouTube and Google queries regarding venom extraction, cobra bite lethality, and sleep sedatives
Recovery of live Russell's viper and spectacled cobra containers and transactions with snake handler Suresh
Chemical forensic identification of sedative drug Clonazepam in the victim's visceral organs
modus_operandi: Purchased venomous snakes (Russell's viper and Indian Spectacled Cobra) from a snake handler. First attempted murder at his own home using a viper, which left victim hospitalized. Subsequently visited victim at her parents' house, slipped sedatives into fruit juice, and intentionally provoked the cobra by pressing its fangs into the sleeping victim's forearm, attempting to frame the death as accidental natural snakebite.
personality_disorder: Forensic psychiatric profiling indicated narcissistic and psychopathic traits: complete affective flattening, meticulous pre-planning of an unconventional biological weapon, and relentless pursuit of victim's gold dowry and financial insurance proceeds.
common_traits: Using biological agents (venomous reptiles) to disguise premeditated murder as accident
Administering chemical sedatives to suppress victim defensive reflexes
Digital preparation and lethal methodology searches on internet
Financial motivation driven by dowry and property appropriation
summary: Historic Indian forensic trial where the prosecution proved murder via snakebite through herpetological experiments, fang-mark distance analysis, and smartphone forensic history. The Sessions Court awarded double life imprisonment, hailed as an investigative triumph for circumstantial scientific evidence.
